argv:
Rewrite the text following the principles of Simplified Technical English.

Use one topic per sentence. Keep procedural sentences to twenty words or
fewer and descriptive sentences to twenty-five words or fewer. Keep paragraphs
to six sentences or fewer.

Use the active voice. Address the reader directly with the imperative for
instructions. Use only the simple present, simple past, and simple future
tense.

Use one word for one meaning throughout, and one meaning for one word: never
vary a term for elegance. Prefer short, common words over long or technical
ones. Do not use noun clusters of more than three words. Write out what a
pronoun refers to whenever there is any doubt.

Do not use slang, idioms, or metaphors.

request.user_prompt:
Rewrite the passage below according to your style instructions.

Output only the rewritten passage. Do not add a preamble, a title, an
explanation, or any commentary about the changes you made.

<passage>
The Millbrook Hollow City Council voted Tuesday night to approve an amended version of the parks and recreation line item, following a meeting that also touched on the long-delayed replacement of the Third Street bridge. According to a spokesperson for the mayor's office, the revised figure reflects "ongoing conversations" among council members, though the spokesperson declined to characterize those conversations further. A separate memo, attributed by two council staffers to the finance subcommittee, put the adjustment at approximately $340,000, a figure that a budget analyst who reviewed the memo said was "in the range we expected." Buried near the end of that same memo, and not raised by any council member during the meeting, was a line noting that the bridge's lead structural engineer had flagged a load-bearing crack serious enough to warrant closing the span to truck traffic within 90 days. The bridge project, which has appeared on the capital plan since at least 2019 and has already drawn 14 change orders, was not discussed in detail. Council member Dana Okafor, reached after the meeting, said only that "the process worked the way it's supposed to work, and I think residents should feel good about that."
</passage>

response.text:
The Millbrook Hollow City Council met on Tuesday night. The council voted to approve an amended version of the parks and recreation line item. The meeting also covered the long-delayed replacement of the Third Street bridge.

A spokesperson for the mayor's office said the revised figure reflects "ongoing conversations" among council members. The spokesperson did not describe those conversations further.

Two council staffers said the finance subcommittee wrote a separate memo. The memo put the adjustment at approximately $340,000. A budget analyst reviewed the memo. The analyst said the figure was "in the range we expected."

The memo also contained a line near its end. No council member raised this line during the meeting. The line stated that the bridge's lead structural engineer had found a load-bearing crack. The engineer said the crack was serious. The engineer recommended closing the bridge to truck traffic within 90 days.

The bridge project has appeared on the capital plan since at least 2019. The project has already received 14 change orders. The council did not discuss the bridge project in detail.

A reporter spoke with council member Dana Okafor after the meeting. Okafor said only that "the process worked the way it's supposed to work." Okafor also said residents should feel good about that.
